llm.summary: This skill is review-worthy because it directs the agent to run an unpinned npm real-estate CLI that can handle API keys and local configuration, though the artifacts do not show clearly malicious behavior.

dimensions.detail: A mutable third-party npm package would run with the agent user's local privileges and may receive an API key; that authority is not tightly scoped by the skill artifact.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The metadata and examples use npx -y xiaolu-house without an exact package version, lockfile, integrity hash, or bundled reviewed implementation.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The instructions tell the agent to execute all xiaolu-house npx commands for the user, call help before queries, include promotional mini-program links, and expose config commands without clear consent checkpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill discloses persistent storage under ~/.xiaolu-house/config and provides set/show/clear operations, but does not document confirmation, redaction, or storage verification controls.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The real-estate search purpose is coherent, but the skill expands that purpose into agent-executed CLI commands, API-key setup, user/config display, and config clearing.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review before installing. Only use this skill if you trust the xiaolu-house npm package and publisher, prefer a pinned reviewed version, use a limited API key, and require confirmation before showing or clearing saved configuration.
llm.findings:
[RP1] unexpected: Accepted in substance: repeated npx -y xiaolu-house invocations are unpinned and agent-directed, creating mutable remote-code execution risk; this is not evidence that the current package is compromised.
[SQP-1] expected: Downgraded: broad property-search triggers match the stated purpose, and the skill says to clarify ambiguous intent before proceeding.
[SQP-2] expected: Partially accepted: config show and clear are normal configuration features, but showing user information and clearing persisted settings need stronger user confirmation and redaction guidance.
[SQP-3] expected: Downgraded: Chinese instructions are coherent for this China-focused housing service and are not a security concern by themselves.
[T08] unexpected: Accepted: the artifact lacks version pinning or integrity controls for automatic npm execution, including credential-handling commands.
[T01] expected: Partially accepted: mini-program and agent-contact links are related to the commercial real-estate workflow, but the unconditional promotional wording should be disclosed and optional.
